extracted.intended_audience: community groups, place keepers, artists, cultural heritage institutions, museums, public-space stewards, and storytellers seeking Mellon Foundation Humanities in Place funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants to the Mellon Foundation's Humanities in Place program describing what kinds of projects, sites, communities, and applicants the program funds and how the application/inquiry process works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative programming advanced by community groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative programming, advanced by community groups, that seeks to explore and share cultural heritage for broad public benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program supports projects led by community groups that use creative or new approaches to explore and present cultural heritage; emphasis on programming that reaches and benefits broad public audiences rather than serving only narrow or internal constituencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiatives focusing on often-overlooked communities or regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives that focus on often-overlooked communities or regions to broaden our understanding of American and Indigenous histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that centers histories and perspectives that have been marginalized or overlooked; projects should demonstrably broaden public knowledge of American and Indigenous histories and geographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for cultural heritage sites that promote access and exchange of stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural heritage sites, including museums and public spaces, that promote greater access and exchange of stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding targets sites and places (museums, public spaces, etc.) that actively increase accessibility and facilitate exchange among community members and visitors about place-based stories and histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering place keepers, artists, institutions, and storytellers who spotlight overlooked sites
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund place keepers, artists, institutions, and storytellers who shine a spotlight on historically overlooked sites, and the communities and stories that surround them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should be led by or meaningfully engage individuals and organizations with deep knowledge or stewardship of place (place keepers, artists, storytellers), and should draw attention to the people and stories tied to historically overlooked sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic aim: broaden shared understanding and foster mutual learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should help broaden our shared understanding and open new paths to discover what unites us, what makes us unique, and what we can learn from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are evaluated on their potential to create connections across communities, highlight both commonalities and distinctiveness, and enable public learning and dialogue rather than narrowly framed or purely academic outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and invitation process (rolling inquiries; staff engagement; invitations to apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Our staff review inquiry submissions and seek out and get to know organizations before inviting them to submit a proposal for funding. Most Mellon grants are made through these invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should submit inquiries rather than full proposals initially; expectation that program staff will engage with organizations, assess fit, and extend invitations for full proposals. Direct, unsolicited full proposals may be less typical than invited submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and community scope: communities of all sizes across the United States and territories
rubrics_metrics.description: From Alaska to Guam and the Borderlands to the Midwest, America is a constellation of unique heritages, traditions, and stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program explicitly supports projects across diverse geographies and community sizes throughout the U.S. and territories; applicants from remote, rural, urban, and territorial contexts are within scope.
